title: Tail-aware probabilistic phase orchestrator for latency/throughput balancing
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode allocator favors static phase splits tuned for average load. We observe tail-latency spikes during microbursts and unfair throughput throttling for lower-priority customers when kernel choices change due to sequence-length distribution shifts. Goal: implement an adaptive, probabilistic phase orchestration layer that combines short-term tail-index prediction with attention-cost signals and kernel-affinity hints to dynamically pick phase-splits and microbatch packing strategies.

High-level approach: 1) Collect per-request features at admission (estimated prefix length, attention density estimate from tokenizer heuristics, customer tier, recent tail score from telemetry). 2) Use a lightweight online estimator (exponential tail-index and EWMA of token-cost) to compute a short-term "tail risk" score. 3) Convert tail risk + customer priority into a probabilistic policy that picks among candidate phase splits (no-split, shallow-split, deep-split) and kernel affinity preferences (favor KV-cache-optimized kernel vs low-latency kernel). 4) Feed decisions into the existing microbatch packer with a soft fairness token bucket that ensures long-run proportional throughput while allowing opportunistic hedged fastpaths for low-latency requests. 5) Instrument for rollback: decisions tagged with metadata for tracing and can be overridden by SLA rules.

Why different: unlike deterministic heuristics and pure latency-first strategies used in prior tickets, this policy explicitly models short-term tail risk and exposes a probabilistic knob to trade immediate tail mitigation vs total throughput, reducing oscillations caused by binary phase changes.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator: new policy integrated into existing prefill/decode simulator and validated across 10 anonymized workload traces; 30% reduction in 99.9th latency for high-tail traces without >5% throughput loss for P0 customers.
Runtime: production-compatible decision path implemented in C++/Rust runtime with <200ns median admission overhead and feature-gating via remote config.
Observability: per-decision telemetry (chosen-split,kernel-hint,tail-score) emitted and dashboards added to Console showing fairness over time and tail-latency heatmaps.
Safety: canary rollout plan defined with auto-fallback to current deterministic allocator on SLA regressions or error rates.
Docs: short runbook and README describing knobs and how to tune probabilistic distributions for customers.
comments: 2026-02-22 Marco: Spike complete — initial simulator prototype (Python) shows promising reductions on two microburst traces. Noise when kernel selection switches rapidly; need kernel-affinity smoothing.

2026-03-01 Priya: Security review asked whether per-customer scoring leaks cross-customer info. Confirmed inputs are local request features and aggregated tail metrics; added privacy note and opt-out flag for PII-sensitive deployments.

2026-03-04 Engineering review: Suggest caching computed tail-score for 50ms to avoid high-cost recomputation when a request is immediately retried; also add deterministic fallback path for exact-SLA requests.
2026-03-09 Marco: Implemented C++ decision path and unit tests. Admission overhead measured at ~180ns median on e2e bench (x86 server). Pushing WIP PR.
2026-03-11 QA: Load test under mixed tenant scenario (5 tenants, mixed seq-len) shows long-run proportional fairness within 2.8% deviation; 99.9p improved for two high-tail tenants by 27%.
2026-03-13 Priya: Preparing canary flag and console dashboard panels; scheduling canary rollout for 2026-03-20 to a subset of Dedicated pools during low-traffic window.
